details: Michael Saylor's MicroStrategy announced a $12.54 billion net loss in the first quarter of 2026, primarily due to a $14.46 billion unrealized loss on its substantial Bitcoin holdings of 818,334 BTC. This development has contributed to negative sentiment for Bitcoin in May 2026, raising concerns about the stability and valuation of institutional Bitcoin investments.
title: MicroStrategy Q1 Net Loss Driven by $14.46B Bitcoin Unrealized Loss

details: Easing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and strong U.S. macroeconomic data have reduced market-wide risk aversion, leading to a rebound in equities and Bitcoin, which surpassed $81,000. Concurrently, tokenization projects are accelerating, with multiple institutions advancing initiatives to make on-chain assets foundational for global liquidity.
title: Geopolitical Calm & Tokenization Boost Bitcoin, Risk Assets

details: The U.S. economy grew at an annualized rate of 2.0% in Q1 2026, a rebound from 0.5% in Q4 2025, supported by private investment, particularly in AI-related equipment, and government spending. Despite this growth, inflation remains elevated, with March CPI at 3.3% year-over-year. Federal Reserve officials are increasingly expressing hawkish views, with some dissenting against an easing bias due to persistent inflation risks from rising oil prices and broad-based price pressures.
sourceName: U.S. Department of the Treasury / Business Insider
title: US Q1 GDP Grows 2.0%; Inflation Remains High, Fed Officials Hawkish

details: Crypto investors are watching upcoming U.S. economic releases closely, including the April Nonfarm Payrolls on May 8 and April CPI data on May 12. Stronger-than-expected jobs data or higher inflation could diminish expectations for Fed rate cuts, negatively impacting crypto liquidity. Additionally, Coinbase will release its Q1 2026 earnings after market close on May 7, which is viewed as a key indicator for overall crypto trading volumes.
title: April Jobs, CPI Data, and Coinbase Earnings to Influence Crypto

details: Bank of America anticipates Mexico's central bank (Banxico) will reduce its policy rate by 25 basis points to 6.50% on May 7. This decision is expected despite elevated inflation levels exceeding the central bank's target and ongoing economic uncertainty. The bank forecasts the terminal rate to remain at 6.50% for the rest of 2026.
title: Banxico Expected to Cut Rates Amid Inflation and Uncertainty
